title: Trinity nuclear test
summary: In the early morning of 16 July 1945 a plutonium implosion device nicknamed the Gadget, raised on a 100-foot tower, was detonated on the Alamogordo Bombing Range in New Mexico's Jornada del Muerto, in the world's first nuclear explosion; yield is given as 15 to 20 kilotons. The Tularosa Basin Downwinders say fallout harmed nearby residents, and little was done to assess their health.

uncertainty.note: DOE gives 5:30 a.m.; the Atomic Heritage Foundation gives 5:29:45 a.m.

where.modern_name: Trinity Site, White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico, USA
where.historical_name: Alamogordo Bombing Range (Jornada del Muerto), New Mexico, United States

importance.justification: First detonation of a nuclear weapon.

audience_note: Includes the claim that nearby residents were exposed to fallout without health assessment; sources describe cancers and deaths reported by downwinders.

sources.title: Trinity Site: World's First Nuclear Explosion
Trinity Test, 1945
sources.publisher: Atomic Heritage Foundation (National Museum of Nuclear Science & History)

reviewer_note: Sources differ on the time (5:29:45 versus 5:30) and give 18.6 kt (DOE) versus 15-20 kt (AHF); the summary gives only the range. The downwinder harm is the group's claim, reported as such.
